questions.question: If an aggressive driver confronts you, what should you do?

options.text: Move out of their way.
Do not make eye contact.
Do not respond to their hand gestures.
All of the above.

questions.explanation: If an aggressive driver confronts you, move out of their way. Do not make eye contact. Do not respond to their gestures. Never try to challenge aggressive drivers by speeding up.

questions.question: What happens if one-fourth of a vehicle's leaf spring leaves are missing during inspection?

options.text: The driver can drive, but only at reduced speeds.
The vehicle cannot be driven until it is fixed.
The vehicle is safe to drive because most of the spring is still there.
The driver must reduce the weight of the load.

questions.correctAnswerText: The vehicle cannot be driven until it is fixed.
questions.explanation: If one-fourth or more of the leaf spring leaves are missing, the vehicle cannot be driven until the spring is fixed.

questions.question: If you must drive very slowly, what should you do?

options.text: Warn other drivers.
Drive on the shoulder.
Stay in the left lane.
Use your horn.

questions.explanation: If you must drive slowly, warn drivers behind you by turning on your emergency flashers, if local law allows it.

questions.question: To make your vehicle more visible during the day, you should:

options.text: Use your low beam headlights.
Use your high beam headlights.
Use your clearance lights.

questions.explanation: Use low beam headlights for the best visibility during the day. High beam headlights can be dangerous around other drivers.

questions.question: Is it allowed to carry gases or liquids in a leaking tank?

options.text: It is not a good idea.
It is okay on short trips.
It is illegal.
It is okay on rural roads.

questions.explanation: Before driving, check the tank for dents or cracks. Check around and under the vehicle for leaks. Carrying gases or liquids in a leaking tank is illegal.

questions.question: What is true about hydroplaning?

options.text: It rarely happens with large trucks.
It usually happens when vehicles travel faster than 65 mph.
It can happen with only a small amount of water on the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: It can happen with only a small amount of water on the road.
questions.explanation: Hydroplaning occurs when tires lose grip on the road and slide on a layer of water. You do not need a lot of water on the road for hydroplaning to happen.

questions.question: When driving under a bridge or overpass, what should you assume about the posted clearance height?

options.text: The posted height is correct.
The posted height may not be correct.
You should measure the opening before driving through.

questions.correctAnswerText: The posted height may not be correct.
questions.explanation: Do not assume posted height clearances are accurate. If the road was repaved or there is snow on the ground, the actual height may be different. If you are unsure your vehicle can fit, slow down and find another route if possible.

questions.question: Hazardous materials should be loaded:

options.text: Near heat sources.
Away from heat sources.
In direct sunlight.
In the rain.

questions.explanation: Always load hazardous materials away from heat sources. Many materials become more dangerous when heated.

questions.question: Before loading or unloading flammable liquids, the engine should be:

options.text: Off.
Running at high speed.
On.

questions.explanation: Turn off the engine before loading or unloading flammable liquids, unless the engine must run to operate a pump. Ground the tank before opening the filling hole and keep it grounded until the hole is closed.

questions.question: Most heavy vehicles require ____ to change gears.

options.text: Double clutching
Double shifting
Triple clutching
Triple shifting

questions.explanation: Most heavy vehicles with manual transmissions use double clutching to change gears. Release the accelerator, push in the clutch, and shift to neutral at the same time. Release the clutch and let the vehicle reach the needed speed. Then push in the clutch again, shift gears, and release the clutch while accelerating.

questions.question: When carrying Division 1.1 explosives, how far must you park from the nearest building?

options.text: 10 feet
50 feet
300 feet

questions.explanation: When carrying Division 1.1, 1.2, or 1.3 explosives, you must park at least 300 feet away from bridges, tunnels, and buildings. You may park closer only for short periods when you need to do something necessary, like refueling.

questions.question: What is a benefit of inspecting your vehicle?

options.text: It is a waste of time.
It helps find small problems before they become big ones.
The driver should not do it.
It should be done once a month.

questions.correctAnswerText: It helps find small problems before they become big ones.
questions.explanation: Inspect your vehicle before every trip. This helps you find small problems before they turn into serious ones. It is better to find a problem before you drive than after you start.

questions.question: Are shipping papers required?

options.text: No, not for most shipments.
Yes, for all shipments.
They should be stored in a special spot in the cab.
They can be kept as a digital file only.

questions.explanation: Shipping papers are required for all hazardous material shipments. They tell drivers and dock workers about the dangers of the cargo.

questions.question: When must you use a "Poison Inhalation Hazard" placard?

options.text: Only when carrying more than 100 pounds.
Only when carrying more than 50 pounds.
For any amount of the product.
Only if the container is leaking.

questions.correctAnswerText: For any amount of the product.
questions.explanation: When carrying materials that need a "Poison Inhalation Hazard" placard, you must display it and the correct hazard class placard. This applies even for small amounts.

questions.question: When turning left at an intersection with two turn lanes, which lane should you use?

options.text: Use the right lane.
Either lane is fine.
Use the left lane.

questions.explanation: You may need to swing right to make a safe left turn. When two left turn lanes are available, always start your turn in the right lane.

questions.question: What danger can happen when a large truck swerves to avoid a hazard?

options.text: The truck may miss the object.
The truck may flip over.
The truck may stay in the same lane.
Other vehicles may do the same thing.

questions.explanation: Swerving is sometimes safer than stopping. You can turn away from something faster than you can stop. However, if your vehicle is top-heavy or pulling trailers, swerving can cause a rollover.

questions.question: How should you drive a tank on curves?

options.text: Faster than the posted speed limit.
Slower than the posted speed limit.
Use both lanes if there are two lanes of traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slower than the posted speed limit.
questions.explanation: Tank vehicles have a high center of gravity and roll over easily. Drive well below the speed limit on curves to prevent rollover.

questions.question: When driving on packed snow, how much should you reduce your speed?

options.text: By at least one-half.
By about one-third.
By about one-quarter.
By about one-eighth.

questions.explanation: Reduce your speed by one-half or more on packed snow. Slippery surfaces make it hard to stop and turn, so you must drive slower to stay safe.

questions.question: What sign could mean cargo contains hazardous materials?

options.text: The cargo is in cylinder tanks.
The cargo is from a supermarket.
The cargo is on wood pallets.

questions.correctAnswerText: The cargo is in cylinder tanks.
questions.explanation: Cylinders and drums often contain hazardous materials. Use proper safety steps when transporting hazardous cargo.

questions.question: During a pre-trip inspection, what is the best way to check your lights?

options.text: Park near a mirror and look for a reflection.
Turn on the lights, then get out of the vehicle to look at them.
Check the instrument panel for warning lights.
Drive in traffic and wait for other drivers to tell you if lights are out.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn on the lights, then get out of the vehicle to look at them.
questions.explanation: During a pre-trip inspection, turn on your lights and then get out to check them.
